status_reason: The concept is blocked: silica fiber cannot carry mid-IR, and the alternative fiber depends on link length, routing and process conditions that the enquiry does not supply.
answer: The existing silica fiber from the NIR setup cannot carry the mid-IR light needed for MIR ATR of water in oil, so it is not approved for MIR. MIR ATR with a ZrO2 ATR probe is still the method to test first, in the lab, on PIR or CIR fibers. No detection limit can be given from the available sources, and approval needs the fiber type, link length, routing and conditions.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR water-in-oil in the lab first, on PIR or CIR fibers and not the existing silica fiber
inline.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 tip sealed in a PEEK shaft
inline.install: Process location not yet known; to be defined after link length, routing and conditions are supplied
inline.fiber: PIR (3-17 µm) or CIR (1.1-6.5 µm) IR fiber
inline.test_against: NIR on the existing silica fiber, as a comparison only
inline.not_final_because: Fiber type, link length, routing, process conditions and the required accuracy or detection limit are not supplied, and the slide gives no detection limit.

problems.text: Silica fiber from the NIR setup transmits only about 350-2400 nm, and MIR starts at 4000 cm-1 (2.5 µm), so the existing silica fiber cannot carry MIR ATR light.
The water-in-oil spectra in the slides cover 4000-2000 cm-1 (MIR), so they cannot be reproduced with the NIR silica route.
Approval cannot be given yet: the fiber type, link length, routing and conditions are not supplied, and method selection depends on these factors.
The requested 0.01 % detection limit is not in the sources; the water-in-oil slide gives no detection limit and only shows 0.1 %, 0.5 %, 1.0 % and 2.0 % water.

methods.why: ATR probes with ZrO2 tips are used for water in petroleum, and absorbance rises with water content in 4000-2000 cm-1; MIR ATR is suited to liquid and paste samples.
NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method and fits the existing NIR setup, but its overlapping bands require chemometrics.
Raman is complementary to MIR but needs special probes, and its signals can be masked by fluorescence.
Fluorimetry relies on secondary emission of certain substances, mostly biological, and most chemicals do not fluoresce.

questions.q: What is the fiber link length from the probe to the spectrometer, and how is the fiber routed?
questions.why: Fiber type and approval depend on link length and routing.

questions.q: What are the process conditions at the probe (temperature, pressure, flow, and whether the line is hot or pressurised)?
questions.why: Probe and fiber construction depend on conditions; none are given in the source slide.

questions.q: What water content range must be measured, and what accuracy or detection limit is required?
questions.why: No detection limit is given in the sources, and the required performance sets the test design.

questions.q: Is the sample a liquid or a paste, and what is its composition (crude or refined, other components)?
questions.why: ATR suits liquid and soft samples, and unknown composition can change which method works.

questions.q: Is a MIR-capable FTIR spectrometer available for the lab test?
questions.why: The MIR ATR test needs a spectrometer that covers 4000-2000 cm-1.

experiment.objective: Check whether MIR ATR with a ZrO2 probe on PIR or CIR fiber can quantify water in petroleum over the range shown in the source, and whether a NIR comparison adds value.
steps: Prepare water-in-oil reference samples across the range shown in the source (0.1 % to 2.0 % water), with reference values from independent laboratory analyses.
Measure the samples with the ZrO2 ATR probe on a PIR or CIR fiber across 4000-2000 cm-1, after checking the fiber transmits at 2.5 µm and above over the planned link length.
Split the samples into calibration and independent validation sets, and build a chemometric model on the calibration set only.
Repeat the measurements with the NIR route on the existing silica fiber as a comparison, using the same validation set.
Judge the MIR model against the NIR comparison and the client's own criteria.
references: AFS slide on water in petroleum, S02 p.13
AFS fiber transmission table, S02 p.6

pathway.key_features: Water-related absorbance rise in the 4000-2000 cm-1 MIR region (S02 p.13 example spectra).
pathway.path_reason: The lab test and the missing fiber, link and process facts must come first.

multispectral.why: Raman is complementary to MIR, and oil is named as a complex medium that may need two or more methods.
multispectral.test: Only after MIR ATR alone is tested: the combination must beat the best single method on the same independent validation data.

assumptions: The line carries petroleum oil with water present.
The water content lies within the 0.1 % to 2.0 % range shown in the source slide.
Link length, routing, temperature, pressure and flow are unknown and are not assumed.
